_comment: BACKWARD-COMPATIBILITY FIXTURE. The CURRENT format is NRM-2 and its fixture is the file
beside this one, nrm2-sample.json; nothing writes an NRM-1 document any more.
This one is kept, and kept passing, because a map somebody downloaded before 2026-07-29 is
the only copy they have and it must still open years from now. Its parts carry no
part_index, which is exactly what NRM-1 looks like: 'the field is absent' is legal here and
is a refusal in an NRM-2 document (RECOVERY-MANIFEST.md 2.1, 6). That difference is the
whole reason both files exist rather than one.
Rust  : nmts/crypto/tests/api.rs            (what the standalone recovery tool will parse)
Both sides compare PARSED values, not bytes, so key order is free; field names and shapes
are not. Keys beginning with _ are documentation and are ignored by both parsers.
Covers: the chain fields, a multi-part file with no quilt, a quilted file, an item with no
content hash (committed before hashes existed), a part with no Sui object id, a part that
NAMES its storage network, and a part that omits it (= walrus, what pre-field maps look like).
The 'filecoin' value below is a FORMAT PROBE, not a claim that anything is stored there — a
non-default name is what stops either side passing this test with 'walrus' hardcoded.
